sections.title: Sound of the letter C
paragraphs: The letter (C) /siː/ has two sounds. Its main sound is a consonant in the word (cat) /kæt/, which means a small pet that meows. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. You will hear both sounds across many common words.

sections.title: How to say the sounds
paragraphs: To make the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to touch the roof. Trap the air completely, then let it burst out. For the second sound, place your tongue tip near the tooth ridge. Blow air through the narrow gap to make a hiss. Keep your voice off. Put your hand on your throat to check that it does not shake.

sections.title: When to use each sound
paragraphs: You say the first sound before the letters a, o, u, or any consonant. You hear this in (cup) /kʌp/. You say the second sound before the letters e, i, or y. You hear this in (city) /sɪt.i/, and also in the word (cell) /sɛl/.

sections.title: Common mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not voice these sounds. In the word (cat) /kæt/, do not use the heavy sound of go. In the word (city) /sɪt.i/, do not say the buzzing sound of zoo. Keep the throat quiet, and blow pure air without your voice.
